summary: Refactored GetPluginsDiffAsync in DiffService.cs to use the LCS pipeline: calls FileService.ReadModListAsync (twice — reference and current), ComputeLcs, then ClassifyChanges. The old FileService.GetModDiffAsync call and the DetectReplacements + DetectAndAssignDependentChanges calls are gone.
Added public static ReadModListAsync(string filePath, bool isReferenceFile = false) to FileService.cs as a thin delegate to the private ReadFileAsync, returning Task<IReadOnlyList<ModEntryModel>>.
Removed DetectReplacements (was L574–L632) and DetectAndAssignDependentChanges (was L132–L236) from DiffService.cs.

Fixed a correctness bug in ClassifyChanges Step 3 (replacement detection): cumulativeDeletions now only increments for true removals, not for replacements. This ensures that multiple consecutive replacements at adjacent reference positions are all correctly matched.

Fixed ClassifyChanges Step 6 (dependent-change attribution): replaced the greedy 'first causal match' loop with a range-based attribution that mirrors the old DetectAndAssignDependentChanges logic — each removed entry owns the range from its reference position + 1 up to (but not including) the next removal's reference position.
Added a final reference-position sort to ClassifyChanges output to match the ordering produced by the old implementation (which iterated diffs sorted by ReferenceNumber then CurrentNumber).
Updated Scenario16 test: removed the FALLBACK branch; the test now asserts only the IDEAL replacement-detected behavior since the LCS pipeline always succeeds.
Deleted DetectReplacementsTests.cs (reflection-based test for the removed DetectReplacements method).

Test results: 430 total, 406 pass, 24 fail. All 24 failures are pre-existing locale issues on the French test system (fr-FR vs en-US) — not caused by these changes. The DiffServiceTests, ScenarioTests (all 16), and FileServiceTests all pass.

comments.note: DiffService.cs ClassifyChanges Step 3 had a correctness bug in the original WP-001 implementation: cumulativeDeletions was incremented for every removed item including replacements. This meant two consecutive replacements (e.g. Scenario 09) would incorrectly miss the second and subsequent replacements. Fixed by only incrementing for unmatched (true) removals.

DiffService.cs ClassifyChanges Step 6 had an incorrect dependent-change attribution strategy: it assigned ALL shifted LCS items to the first causal removal they followed, so only the earliest removal accumulated dependents. Fixed by using the same range-based attribution as the removed DetectAndAssignDependentChanges — each removal owns items between its position and the next removal.

ClassifyChanges result ordering was non-deterministic relative to the old implementation because Moved entries from same-filename reconciliation and from lcsShifted were added in different sections. Added a final reference-position sort to maintain the expected ordering observed by Assert.Collection tests.

ReplacementDetectionDiagnostics.cs (Tests/LoadOrderKeeper.Tests/) still exists as a diagnostic test file that manually simulates the old DetectReplacements algorithm inline. It still passes (calls GetPluginsDiffAsync and asserts Replaced) but its narrative log comments are now stale — they describe the two-pass heuristic rather than the LCS pipeline. Consider updating or removing this file in a follow-up.

DiffService.cs is missing a top-level using directive for System.IO — the file compiles because the System.IO.File calls are qualified by the existing implicit global usings, but the explicit 'using System.IO;' at line 1 of the original file appears to have been intentionally included. After the refactor the only remaining direct System.IO usage is File.Exists — verify the using is still needed (it is, for File.Exists).

comments.note: DiffServiceTests.GetPluginsDiffAsync_DetectsReplacements asserts Assert.Contains('line 2', entry.Text). On this fr-FR system the localized text is 'b.esm remplacé par c.esm à la ligne 2', so 'line 2' is not found. This is a pre-existing locale-insensitive test — the replacement is detected correctly (ChangeType.Replaced, b.esm, c.esm all pass). The test should use Assert.Contains('2', entry.Text) or be decorated with a culture-override fixture. Not a regression from this WP.

ReplacementDetectionDiagnostics.cs remains in the test project with stale narrative comments describing the old two-pass heuristic. Its assertions still pass against the new LCS pipeline. Consider deleting or rewriting its comments in a follow-up — pre-flagged by Developer as low-priority debt.

Edge case: ClassifyChanges Step 3 newByCurPos uses LineNumber as key with a guard for pos==0. If a mod entry has LineNumber=null (e.g. ReadModListAsync called with a non-standard path that skips line assignment), those entries would be silently excluded from replacement matching and fall through as Added. This is a pre-existing design decision in ReadFileAsync (logicalIndex always increments for enabled entries), so no actual risk in current code paths.

comments.note: DiffService.cs ClassifyChanges final sort comparator: added a 2-line comment above 'int xKey = x.ReferenceNumber ?? int.MaxValue' to explain the int.MaxValue sentinel. The sentinel ensures null-ReferenceNumber entries (pure Added mods) sort after all reference-positioned entries. Without the comment the choice of int.MaxValue reads as an arbitrary magic number. Non-behavioral change — sort output is identical.

DiffService.cs ClassifyChanges Step 1 vs Step 3 LineNumber fallback inconsistency: Step 1 (lcsShifted build) uses 'ri + 1' as the null-LineNumber fallback, while Step 3 (newByCurPos build) uses '0' and explicitly skips pos==0 entries. In practice ReadFileAsync always assigns LineNumber, so this is latent-only. For long-term resilience, both steps should use a consistent fallback strategy (either both sentinel-0-and-skip, or both index+1). Consider aligning in a follow-up.

DiffService.cs ClassifyChanges Step 6b (insertion attribution): the firstAffected lookup inside the foreach(inserted) loop performs shiftedByRefPos.Where(...).OrderBy(...) on every iteration — O(k log k) per inserted entry, O(k^2) overall for k shifted items. For current mod list sizes (hundreds) this is not measurable, but a two-pointer or sorted-index approach would be O(k). Flag for future optimization if mod list sizes grow significantly.

DiffService.cs ClassifyChanges Step 6: shiftedByRefPos is built with .Where(s => s.ReferenceNumber.HasValue) but shiftedLines always assigns a non-null ReferenceNumber (it is set from refPos in the lcsShifted loop at Step 1). The .Where filter is vacuously always true. Consider removing it or replacing with a Debug.Assert to make the invariant explicit.
